en: The Sūtra on Maitreya’s Descent and Attainment of Buddhahood, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Yijing by Imperial Command.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha.
Together with a great assembly of bhikṣus, at that time Śāriputra—

the one of great wisdom and foremost among the generals of the Dharma— out of compassion for the world, rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One!..."
"I now wish to inquire briefly; I pray that you will grant me your attention!
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Ask whatever you wish, and I shall explain it for you."
Then Śāriputra addressed the World-Honored One with these verses:
“The Great Teacher has bestowed a prophecy That a Buddha shall descend to birth in the future;
His name shall be Maitreya, Just as it was spoken in the sūtras of the past and present.”
"I only pray that the Honored One among Men will further analyze this in verse;
I now desire to hear of his supernormal powers and majestic virtue.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"You should listen with a sincere and attentive mind;
in the future, the Honored One Maitreya shall proclaim it extensively for you.
At that time, the waters of the great ocean will gradually diminish by three thousand [yojanas]."
Two hundred yojanas [in width] manifest the path of the Wheel-Turning King;
Jambudvīpa is ten thousand yojanas in length and breadth,
and sentient beings dwell within it, filling every place.
The land is entirely prosperous and flourishing, free from punishments and calamities;
those men and women therein are all born of virtuous karma.
The earth has no thorns, producing only soft, green grass.
Treading upon the footsteps of others is like beholding fine cotton wool;
fragrant rice grows spontaneously, and all delicious flavors are fully provided.
From the various trees grow garments, adorned with a multitude of colors.
The trees reach a height of three krosas, their flowers and fruits always abundant;
the people of that land all have a lifespan of eighty thousand years.
Free from all illness and suffering, they dwell in constant peace and happiness, devoid of affliction.
All their physical marks were perfectly dignified, and their complexion and strength were fully perfected.
Human beings there have three kinds of ailments: hunger, old age, and excrement.
Women do not enter into marriage until they are five hundred years of age.
For all who wish to relieve themselves, the earth cracks open to receive them;
when their lives are about to end, they go of their own accord to the charnel ground.
The city is named Citradhvaja-lakṣaṇa, the capital of a wheel-turning monarch.
Twelve yojanas in length, And seven yojanas in breadth;
Those who dwell therein Have all planted wondrous causes.
This city possesses supreme virtues, And all its inhabitants rejoice.
The towers and terraces, including the defensive walls, are composed of the seven treasures;
the locks, keys, gates, and courtyards are all adorned with various jewels.
The ramparts and surrounding moats are all constructed of exquisite gems.
Famous flowers fill it completely, and beautiful birds all alight and gather there.
Seven rows of *tāla* trees surround it on every side;
adorned with various jewels, they are all hung with nets and small bells.
A gentle breeze blows through the jewel trees, producing a multitude of wondrous sounds;
like the performance of the eight musical instruments, those who hear them give rise to joy.
Everywhere there are ponds and pools, covered with flowers of various colors.
Gardens and groves sprout fragrant trees, adorning these city walls.
Within the land dwells a holy sovereign, whose name is Śaṅkha;
a Wheel-Turning King of the four continents, prosperous, flourishing, and possessed of great power.
That king’s meritorious deeds were vast; he was valiant and commanded the fourfold army.
He had perfected the seven treasures and was fully endowed with a thousand sons.
All within the four seas were pure and tranquil; there were no battles or weapons of war.
The True Dharma governs all living beings, and its transformative influence is entirely impartial.
The King possesses four great treasuries, each located within various kingdoms;
in every single treasury, there are hundreds of billions of precious jewels.
Within the kingdom of Kalinga, there is the treasury named Bingjiele;
in the kingdom of Mithila, there is the great treasury of Banzhugu;
the Elapatra treasury is situated in the kingdom of Gandhara.
In the realm of Vārāṇasī, there is a treasury named Śaṅkha.
These four hidden treasures all belong to King Śaṅkha;
sustained by a hundred merits, his karmic fruition is fully realized.
A great minister who assists the state, a Brahmin of pure virtue;
proficient in all four Vedas, he is a master of vast learning who serves as the national preceptor.
Thoroughly versed in various treatises, he is skilled in instruction and possesses the power of dhāraṇī.
In the exegesis of the teachings and in grammar, there was nothing he did not thoroughly master.
He had a daughter named Viśuddhā, who was the wife of a great minister;
her fame was widespread and her appearance was so dignified and beautiful that all who saw her were filled with joy.
The Great Being, Maitreya, took his leave of the Tuṣita Heaven;
he came to entrust himself to that lady as the place for his final birth.
Having conceived this Great Sage, she fulfilled the full ten months.
Thereupon, the Mother of the Compassionate Honored One proceeded to the Wondrous Flower Garden.
Upon reaching that wondrous garden, she neither sat nor lay down;
standing slowly, she grasped a flowering tree, and in an instant gave birth to the Supreme Compassionate Honored One.
At that time, the Most Victorious Honored One, having emerged from his mother’s right side;
like the sun breaking through the clouds, he radiated great light everywhere.
Untainted by the womb, he was like a lotus flower rising above the water.
Light flows throughout the three realms, as all look up to the radiance of Great Compassion.
At the moment of his descent into birth, Śakra, Lord of the Thousand Eyes,
personally bore the Bodhisattva, joyfully encountering the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings.
At this time, the Bodhisattva spontaneously took seven steps;
at every place his feet trod, precious lotus flowers sprang forth.
Surveying the ten directions, he addressed the assembly of devas and humans:
This is my final body; I shall realize nirvana, free from rebirth.
The dragons descend with cool, clear water to bathe the body of Great Compassion;
The devas scatter exquisite flowers, raining them down everywhere throughout the void.
The devas held white parasols to shelter the Great Compassionate Honored One;
each gave rise to a heart of rare wonder as they guarded the Bodhisattva.
The nurses lifted the Bodhisattva, whose body was endowed with the thirty-two marks.
Endowed with every radiance, [the attendants] held it up and presented it to the Mother.
The charioteer advanced the carved palanquin, adorned entirely with jewels;
the mother and son ascended within it, while the various devas together bore the litter.
With a thousand kinds of exquisite music, they led him back to the palace;
as Maitreya entered the capital city, celestial flowers fell like rain.
On the day the Compassionate Honored One was born, all the women who were pregnant likewise gave birth.
May all obtain peace and security of body, and may all give birth to sons of wisdom.
May the Father, the Compassionate Honored One, pure and virtuous, behold his sons’ wondrous countenances;
endowed with the thirty-two marks, their hearts shall give rise to great joy.
The father, relying on the method of divination, knew that his son possessed two destinies:
to remain in the secular world as a wheel-turning monarch, or to leave the home life and attain perfect enlightenment.
Once the Bodhisattva had reached maturity, he felt compassion for all living beings.
Amidst the many sufferings and perilous difficulties, saṃsāra never ceases.
His golden radiance is brilliant; his voice is like that of Mahābrahmā;
his eyes are like blue lotus petals; and all his limbs are perfectly complete.
His height was eighty cubits, and his shoulders measured twenty;
the width of his face was half that of his shoulders, and he was as majestic and handsome as the full moon.
The Bodhisattva was proficient in all arts and sciences, and was skilled in instructing those who came to study under him.
He invited eighty-four thousand youths who were beginning their studies.
At that time, King Śaṅkha erected seven-jeweled banners;
each banner was seventy fathoms high and sixty fathoms wide.
Once the precious banner was completed, the king gave rise to a mind of great renunciation;
he bestowed it upon a brāhmaṇa and established an equal, unrestricted assembly (paṭaha).
At that time, there were several thousand brahmins.
Having obtained this wondrous jeweled banner, it was torn to pieces in a mere instant.
Upon seeing this, the Bodhisattva reflected that all worldly things are likewise so;
bound within the cage of the suffering of birth and death, he sought a way of deliverance.
He prayed with sincerity for the path of quiescent extinction and abandoned the secular world to become a renunciant;
amidst birth, old age, sickness, and death, he sought to rescue beings and enable them to attain liberation.
The World-Honored One of Compassion made this vow: "Eighty-four thousand people [shall follow]."
Simultaneously giving rise to a mind of weary detachment, he practiced the holy life accordingly;
on the very night of his initial resolve, he abandoned the secular world to go forth as a renunciant;
and within that same night, he ascended to the stage of Perfect Enlightenment.
At that time there was a Bodhi tree, named Nāgapuṣpa;
it was four yojanas high, lush and flourishing.
Its branches covered the four directions, providing shade for six krośas.
The Honored One of Great Compassion, Maitreya, Attains perfect enlightenment below;
Most venerable among humans, He possesses the eight qualities of Brahma’s voice;
He preaches the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, Causing them to be free from all afflictions.
Suffering and the source from which suffering arises— All these are utterly extinguished;
By practicing the Eightfold Noble Path, One ascends to the shore of Nirvana.
For the sake of those with pure faith, I have proclaimed these Four Noble Truths.
Having heard this Dharma in accordance with the truth, they shall uphold it with utmost sincerity.
Within the exquisite flower garden, the multitudes will gather like clouds;
for a full hundred yojanas, their retinues will completely fill the space.
When that Cakravartin King Śaṅkha had heard the profound and wondrous Dharma,
he completely renounced all his precious jewels and directed his heart toward the aspiration for renunciation.
Without lingering attachment to the inner palace, he sought the ultimate departure from suffering.
An assembly of eighty-four thousand followed him forth and left the household life.
Furthermore, eighty-four thousand Brahmin youths,
hearing that the King had abandoned worldly life, also came to seek ordination.
The householder minister in charge of the treasury, whose name was Sudhana,
together with his thousand followers, also came forth to seek renunciation.
So too did the precious lady Viśākhā and her other attendants.
An assembly of eighty-four thousand also came forth to seek ordination;
moreover, good men and good women numbering more than a hundred thousand,
having heard the Buddha proclaim the wondrous Dharma, likewise came to seek ordination.
The Honored One among gods and humans, the Greatly Compassionate Holy Lord;
having universally observed the minds of all beings, he expounded the essential Dharma,
addressing the assembly:
"You should know that the compassionate Lord Śākyamuni has taught you to cultivate the True Path so that you may be born into my Dharma in a future life.
Whether with fragrant flowers and garlands, or with banners, pennants, and canopies as adornments,"
Those who make offerings to the Lord of Munis shall be reborn within my Dharma.
Or those who use saffron and aloeswood, or fragrant clay,
to smear and polish the stupas of the Muni shall be reborn within my Dharma.
Some take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, Respectfully and constantly drawing near;
Always practicing all virtuous deeds, They shall be reborn within my Dharma.
Or, within the Buddha’s Dharma, They receive and uphold the various precepts.
Those who guard their precepts well without transgression will, in a future life, enter my Dharma;
or those who give robes and food to the Sangha of the four directions,
as well as excellent medicines, will, in a future life, enter my Dharma.
"Or on the four fast days, or during the month of supernatural powers;
by observing the eightfold precepts, one shall be reborn within my Dharma.
Or, by means of the three types of supernormal knowledge—namely, the power of psychic travel, the power of clairaudience, and the power of telepathy—he provides instruction.
He transformed and guided the assembly of śrāvakas, causing all their afflictions and delusions to be eliminated.
At the first assembly he preached the Dharma, extensively delivering the śrāvakas;
ninety-six billion people were led to transcend the obstacle of affliction.
In the second assembly he preached the Dharma, extensively delivering all the śrāvakas;
ninety-four billion people were caused to cross the ocean of ignorance.
In the third assembly he preached the Dharma, extensively delivering all the śrāvakas.
He caused ninety-two billion people to have their minds well-tamed.
Having turned the Wheel of Dharma three times, humans and devas were everywhere purified;
then, leading his assembly of disciples, he entered the city to beg for alms.
Having entered the City of Sublime Banners, the streets and alleys were all magnificently adorned;
for the sake of making offerings to the Buddha, the heavens rained down *māndārava* flowers.
The Four Heavenly Kings, Brahmā, and the rest of the celestial hosts [all gathered].
Offering incense, flowers, and garlands, they assist the Honored One of Great Compassion.
The gods of great majesty scatter exquisite robes;
in profusion they fill the cities and towns as they gaze up at the Great King of Physicians.
With exquisite jewel incense and flowers, they scattered and sprinkled them upon all the thoroughfares;
treading upon them was like walking on fine cotton wool.
Music and banners lined both sides of the road as they proceeded.
The assembly of Śakra, Lord of Devas and Humans, praised the Greatly Compassionate Honored One:
"Homage to the Honored One among the Heavens! Homage to the Supreme among Men!
Well done, Bhagavat, who is able to take pity upon the world!"
Devas of great majesty and power, who shall become the hosts of the Māra King,
bowed with palms joined in devotion and praised the Teacher.
The Brahmā Kings and the multitudes of devas surrounded him as their retinue.
Each, with the voice of Brahmā, proclaims the subtle and wondrous Dharma.
Within this world, there are many who are arhats;
having eliminated out-flowing karma, they are forever free from the suffering of afflictions.
Humans, devas, nāgas, and spirits, Gandharvas,
asuras, Rākṣasas, and yakṣas— All joyfully made offerings.
At that time, the great assembly Severed their obstacles and eliminated their doubts.
Transcending the flow of birth and death, they skillfully cultivate pure conduct.
At that time, the great assembly, free from attachment and casting aside precious wealth,
with minds devoid of "self" and "mine," skillfully cultivated pure conduct.
At that time, the great assembly Shattered the net of craving;
With minds perfected in meditative concentration, They skillfully cultivated pure conduct.
Maitreya, the Honored One among gods and humans, Out of compassion for all sentient beings;
For a period of sixty thousand years, he will preach the Dharma to deliver sentient beings.
His transformations will fill hundreds of thousands of billions of worlds, causing them to cross the ocean of afflictions;
having rescued all for whom there is a karmic affinity, he shall finally enter the city of Nirvana.
After the Great Compassionate Honored One, Maitreya, has entered parinirvāṇa,
the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a full sixty thousand years.
If, within my Dharma, one is able to believe and accept it with a profound mind;
When my future life comes, I shall surely serve the Great Compassionate Honored One.
If there are those of wisdom who hear such words as these,
who would not give rise to joy and vow to meet the Honored One Maitreya?

"If those who seek liberation wish to encounter the assembly at the Dragon Flower [Maitreya’s] gathering, they should constantly make offerings to the Triple Gem; they ought to be diligent and never indolent.
At that time, after the World-Honored One had prophesied the future matters concerning Maitreya for Śāriputra and the great assembly, he further addressed Śāriputra:

“If there are sons or daughters of good family who, having heard this Dharma, receive, uphold, read, recite, explain it to others, practice according to its teaching, make offerings of incense and flowers, and transcribe the sutra scrolls—these people shall, in a future age, certainly encounter the descent of Maitreya and all receive his salvation within the three assemblies.”

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking these verses, Śāriputra and the great assembly received them with joy and faith, receiving them upon their heads and putting them into practice.

According to the *Kaiyuan Lu*, there were six translations of the *Maitreya’s Descent and Attainment of Buddhahood Sūtra* (*Mile xiasheng chengfo jing*), three of which were preserved and three lost; this present version is one of those three preserved works. Thus, the fact that this sūtra was absent from the Song Canon was merely a case of its being lost; it has now been recovered from the Dan (Tang) Canon and included here.
